title: Introduction
what_we_take: the format H=(C,F,D,G); modes, timers and counters as state; hysteresis and temporal regularisation; equivalent-looking formulations that differ in robustness

title: The solution concept
what_we_take: hybrid time (t,j): the trace's timestamps and sequence numbers; how maximal solutions end (run on, stall, leave the set) as a deadlock checklist; dwell-time and token-bucket generators as event-rate bounds
key_results: Def 2.3, 2.6; Prop 2.10, 2.11; Ex 2.15 (average dwell time = token bucket)

title: Uniform asymptotic stability, initial treatment
what_we_take: Lyapunov-type certificates on flows and jumps; relaxed conditions where the function may rise in one regime if the other dominates; elapsed hybrid time t+j
key_results: §3.2, §3.3 (relaxed conditions); stability of flows and jumps separately does not give stability of the combination (Ex 3.34–3.36)

title: Perturbations and generalized solutions
what_we_take: the Krasovskii regularisation is the set of behaviours vanishing state perturbations can produce; hysteresis makes decisions on noisy *measurements* robust. Our admission guard is an exact integer test, not such a measurement, so this applies to future adaptive policies (corrected after review)
key_results: Prop 4.10; Thm 4.17 (Hermes = Krasovskii, under local boundedness); Ex 4.18, 4.19

title: Set-valued analysis
what_we_take: the right notion of closeness for traces: jump times may shift (graphical convergence, (τ,ε)-closeness), so compare runs by that, not pointwise

title: Well-posed hybrid systems
what_we_take: model with closed sets and well-behaved maps (the hybrid basic conditions) and predictions are robust; uniform bounds on events per unit time

title: Asymptotic stability, in depth
what_we_take: Ex 7.35: for a constrained inclusion on a compact flow set under the basic conditions with no complete solutions, a smooth remaining-time bound exists. It motivates searching for an upper certificate of a suitably regular model; it does not make our bottleneck maximum one (that is a lower bound: corrected after ChatGPT's review). Robustness results apply to steady-state models only
key_results: Ex 7.6 (finite-time convergence), Ex 7.35; Cor 7.27 (slow parameter drift), Cor 7.28 (slow switching)

title: Invariance principles
what_we_take: where a long run settles without a strict decrease: the steady regime as the largest weakly invariant set where nothing dissipates; single-run (meagre-limsup) versions

title: Conical approximation
what_we_take: homogeneity: how behaviour scales with size; local approximation of switching sets by tangent cones, i.e. reasoning about the knee's geometry rather than fitting a curve
key_results: Lemma 9.3; Thm 9.8; Thm 9.11 (local stability near an equilibrium, not wall-time curvature)
